verses.text: The Song of Songs, Solomon's song.
Let him kiss me with kisses from his own lips. Your love is better than wine.
Your oils smell wonderful. Your name is like oil poured out. No wonder the young women love you.
Take me with you. Let's hurry! The king has brought me into his rooms. Friends: We'll be glad and rejoice in you. We'll praise your love more than wine! Beloved: They're right to love you.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I'm dark and lovely, like Kedar's tents and Solomon's curtains.
Don't stare at me because I'm dark. The sun has scorched me. My mother's sons got angry with me and put me in charge of the vineyards. My own vineyard I haven't kept.
Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where do you graze your flock? Where do you let them rest at noon? Why should I be like a woman in a veil beside your companions' flocks?
If you don't know, most beautiful of women, follow the sheep tracks. Let your young goats graze by the shepherds' tents.
My love, I compare you to a horse pulling one of Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks look beautiful with earrings, and your neck with strings of jewels.
We'll make you gold earrings studded with silver.
While the king was at his table, my perfume filled the air.
My beloved is like a pouch of myrrh resting between my breasts.
My beloved is like a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.
Look at you, my love. You're beautiful, so beautiful. Your eyes are like doves.
Look at you, my beloved. You're beautiful and delightful, and our resting place is green.
The beams of our house are cedar, and the rafters are fir.
I'm a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
Like a lily among thorns, that's how my love stands out among the young women.
Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, that's how my beloved stands out among the young men. I sat in his shade with delight, and his fruit tasted sweet.
He brought me into the banquet hall, and his banner over me is love.
Give me raisins to keep my strength up and apples to refresh me. I'm faint with love.
His left hand is under my head, and his right arm holds me close.
Daughters of Jerusalem, swear to me by the gazelles and the deer of the field. Don't stir up or wake love until it wants to wake.
That's my beloved's voice! Look, here he comes, leaping over the mountains and skipping over the hills.
My beloved is like a gazelle or a young deer. Look, he's standing behind our wall, looking in at the windows and peeking through the lattice.
My beloved spoke to me. “Get up, my love, my beautiful one. Come away with me.
Look, winter is past. The rain is over and gone.
Flowers are showing up across the land. The time for singing is here, and the turtledove's voice is heard in our land.
The fig tree is ripening its green figs. The vines are blooming and giving off their scent. Get up, my love, my beautiful one. Come away with me.”
My dove in the cracks of the rock, in the hidden places of the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice. Your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.
Catch the foxes for us, the little foxes that raid the vineyards, because our vineyards are in bloom.
My beloved is mine and I am his. He grazes among the lilies.
Until the day cools and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved. Be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
At night on my bed, I looked for the one my soul loves. I looked for him, but I couldn't find him.
I'll get up now and go through the city. In the streets and squares I'll look for the one my soul loves. I looked for him, but I couldn't find him.
The watchmen making their rounds in the city found me. “Have you seen the one my soul loves?”
I'd barely passed them when I found the one my soul loves. I held him and wouldn't let him go until I'd brought him into my mother's house, into the room of the woman who conceived me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, swear to me by the gazelles and the deer of the field. Don't stir up or wake love until it wants to wake.
Who's this coming up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense and every kind of spice the merchant sells?
Look, it's Solomon's carriage! Sixty mighty men surround it, some of Israel's mightiest.
They're all skilled with the sword and experienced in war. Each has a sword at his thigh because of the dangers of the night.
King Solomon made himself a carriage out of wood from Lebanon.
He made its posts from silver, its base from gold, and its seat from purple cloth. The daughters of Jerusalem lined its inside with love.
Daughters of Zion, come out and see King Solomon in the crown his mother put on him on his wedding day, the day his heart rejoiced.
Look at you, my love. You're beautiful, so beautiful. Your eyes behind your veil are like doves. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a freshly shorn flock coming up from the wash. Each has twins, and none has lost its young.
Your lips are like scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Your temples behind your veil are like slices of pomegranate.
Your neck is like David's tower, built as an armory. A thousand shields hang on it, all shields of mighty warriors.
Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, feeding among the lilies.
Until the day cools and the shadows flee, I'll go to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense.
You're beautiful all over, my love. There isn't a blemish on you.
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride. Come with me from Lebanon. Look down from the peaks of Amana, Senir, and Hermon, from the lions' dens and the mountains where leopards live.
You've captured my heart, my sister, my bride. You've captured my heart with one glance, with one chain from your necklace.
How beautiful your love is, my sister, my bride! Your love is better than wine, and your perfumes smell better than any spice.
My bride, your lips drip like honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. Your clothes carry the scent of Lebanon.
My sister, my bride, is a locked garden, a locked spring, a sealed fountain.
Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates with choice fruits, with henna and spikenard,
with spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, every kind of incense tree, myrrh and aloes, and all the finest spices,
a fountain for gardens, a well of flowing water, streams that run down from Lebanon.
Wake up, north wind! Come, south wind! Blow through my garden and carry out the scent of its spices. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choice fruits.
I've come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I've gathered my myrrh and my spice, eaten my honeycomb and honey, and drunk my wine and milk. Friends: Eat, friends! Drink your fill, beloved.
I was asleep, but my heart was awake. I heard my beloved knocking. “Open up for me, my sister, my love, my dove, my pure one. My head is covered in dew, my hair damp from the night.”
I've already taken off my robe. Do I have to put it back on? I've washed my feet. Do I have to get them dirty?
My beloved reached his hand through the opening by the latch. My heart pounded for him.
I got up to open the door for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, onto the handles of the lock.
I opened the door for my beloved, but he'd already turned and gone. My heart had gone out to him when he spoke. I looked for him but couldn't find him. I called out, but he didn't answer.
The watchmen on their rounds found me. They beat me and left me bruised. The guards on the walls took my cloak away.
Daughters of Jerusalem, swear to me that if you find my beloved, you'll tell him I'm faint with love.
What makes your beloved better than any other, most beautiful of women? What's so special about him that you'd make us swear like this?
My beloved is fair and ruddy, the finest among ten thousand.
His head is like the purest gold. His hair is thick and black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, washed in milk and set like jewels.
His cheeks are like a bed of spices with mounds of fragrance. His lips are like lilies dripping liquid myrrh.
His hands are like gold rings set with beryl. His body is like carved ivory overlaid with sapphires.
His legs are like marble pillars standing on bases of fine gold. He looks as majestic as Lebanon, as splendid as its cedars.
His mouth is sweetness itself, and he's lovely through and through. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
Where has your beloved gone, most beautiful of women? Which way did he turn? We'll look for him with you.
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to graze his flock in the gardens and gather lilies.
I belong to my beloved, and my beloved belongs to me. He grazes among the lilies.
My love, you're beautiful as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, and awe-inspiring as an army with banners.
Turn your eyes away from me. They've overwhelmed me. Your hair is like a flock of goats resting on the slopes of Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of ewes coming up from the wash. Each has twins, and none has lost its young.
Your temples behind your veil are like slices of pomegranate.
There are sixty queens, eighty concubines, and more young women than anyone can count.

My dove, my perfect one, is one of a kind. She's her mother's only daughter, the favorite of the woman who bore her. The young women saw her and called her blessed. The queens and concubines saw her and praised her.
Who's this who looks out like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, and awe-inspiring as an army with banners?
I went down into the grove of nut trees to see what was growing green in the valley, whether the vines had budded and the pomegranate trees had bloomed.
Before I knew it, my desire had set me among the chariots of my royal people.
Come back, come back, Shulammite! Come back, come back, so we can look at you. Lover: Why do you want to gaze at the Shulammite as though you were watching the dance of Mahanaim?
How beautiful your feet look in sandals, daughter of a prince! Your rounded thighs are like jewels shaped by a skilled artisan.
Your body is like a round goblet that never runs out of mixed wine. Your waist is like a mound of wheat ringed with lilies.
Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon that faces Damascus.
Your head rises like Carmel, and your hair is like purple cloth. The king is held captive in its locks.
How beautiful you are, my love, and what a delight!
You stand tall like a palm tree, and your breasts are like its fruit.
I said, “I'll climb the palm tree and take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of grapes and your breath smell like apples.
Your mouth is like the finest wine, flowing smoothly for my beloved, gliding over the lips of those who sleep.
I belong to my beloved, and he desires me.
Come, my beloved! Let's go out to the fields and spend the night in the villages.
Let's go up early to the vineyards and see whether the vines have budded, the blossoms have opened, and the pomegranates are in bloom. That's where I'll give you my love.
The mandrakes give off their scent. At our doors are all kinds of choice fruits, new and old, that I've saved for you, my beloved.
I wish you were like my brother, who nursed at my mother's breasts. If I found you outside, I'd kiss you, and no one would look down on me.
I'd lead you into my mother's house, where she'd teach me. I'd give you spiced wine to drink, from the juice of my pomegranate.
His left hand would be under my head, and his right hand would hold me close.
Daughters of Jerusalem, swear to me. Don't stir up or wake love until it wants to wake.
Who's that coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Beloved: I woke you under the apple tree. That's where your mother conceived you, where she went into labor and gave birth to you.
Set me like a seal on your heart, like a seal on your arm. Love is strong as death, and jealousy is cruel as Sheol. It flashes like fire, a flame of the LORD himself.
Deep waters can't put out love, and floods can't drown it. If someone offered all the wealth in their house for love, people would reject the offer with contempt.
We have a little sister, and she has no breasts yet. What will we do for her on the day someone asks for her hand?
If she's a wall, we'll build a silver turret on her. If she's a door, we'll enclose her with cedar boards.
I'm a wall, and my breasts are like towers. Then in his eyes I was like someone who'd found peace.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He rented it out to caretakers, and each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.
My own vineyard is before me. The thousand are yours, Solomon, and two hundred go to those who tend its fruit.
You who live in the gardens, with friends listening nearby, let me hear your voice!
Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices!
